title: Asked by Tend: A per-host flake output saying which system services each host runs, for the estate
body:
A per-host flake output saying which system services each host runs, for the estate (graft:01a16034-bfef..6e5c, from Tend)

What was needed:
- Tend: Beside the flake's `configurations` table, an output (e.g. `estate.<hostname>` or `hostServices.<hostname>`) that Tend can read with `nix eval --json <repo>/nix#<output>` without building a system: per host, the system services it turns on, each `{ name, kind = "system", unit? , tailnet_only?, notes? }` (OpenSSH with tailnetOnly and guests, Tailscale, LACT, the Tenstorrent driver, the desktop session, and the like), plus anything about the machine Tend should know that `configurations` doesn't hold (e.g. `hosted_on` for a WSL host). Which options count as a service is yours to decide and keep with the modules that set them; Tend only reads the output.

Answer (done): Done in vg-dotfiles (commit after 3a91d61, not pushed yet). `nix eval --json <repo>/nix#estate` returns, per host (all nixosConfigurations and darwinConfigurations), `{ services = [ { name, kind = "system", unit?, tailnet_only?, notes? } ]; hosted_on? }`, unset fields left out. Each module lists what it turns on where it turns it on (nix/modules/estate.nix declares estate.services): openssh (tailnet_only, key/password, guest account names), tailscale (Tailscale SSH on/off), lact, tenstorrent (tt-kmd version, hugepages), sddm (with its sessions), networkmanager or wpa_supplicant, bluetooth, cups, yabai on macOS. vgwsl2 has hosted_on = "vghydra". Hosts without their hardware-configuration.nix yet (vgnixmini, vgsquid-azul/onyx/jade) answer too: their import is skipped until the file exists. All 7 hosts evaluate in about 10 s. Note for the reader on Windows: run it as `wsl -d NixOS -- bash -lc 'nix eval --json ~/vg-dotfiles/nix#estate'` (nix is only on a login shell's PATH, per graft 01a1619a).
